module.title: Modern Web Development Flow
module.description: Understand how modern websites and fullstack applications are built from frontend to backend.

lessons.title: What Is Frontend?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Frontend is the visible part of a website or app that users interact with directly.

sections.heading: What Users Actually See
sections.content: Buttons, forms, images, dashboards, menus, and pages are all part of the frontend.

sections.heading: Frontend Technologies
sections.content: Frontend is mainly built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

sections.heading: Modern Frontend Frameworks
sections.content: Frameworks like React help developers build faster and more interactive user interfaces.

sections.heading: Frontend Focus
sections.content: Frontend development focuses on user experience, design, responsiveness, and interaction.

easyExample.title: Car Dashboard Example
easyExample.content: Frontend is like a car dashboard. Users interact with buttons, screens, and controls directly.

summary: React is widely used for frontend development

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Backend is the hidden part of an application that handles logic, processing, and data.

sections.heading: What Backend Does
sections.content: Backend handles authentication, databases, APIs, server logic, and security.

sections.heading: Users Cannot See Backend
sections.content: Backend runs on servers behind the scenes and processes requests from frontend applications.

sections.heading: Backend Technologies
sections.content: Backend can be built using Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, and many other technologies.

sections.heading: Backend And Data
sections.content: Backend connects applications with databases and business logic.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Kitchen Example
easyExample.content: Users only see the dining area, but the kitchen secretly prepares everything. Backend works similarly.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Frontend and backend communicate using requests and responses.

sections.heading: How Communication Starts
sections.content: Frontend sends requests when users perform actions like login, signup, or searching.

sections.heading: Backend Processes Requests
sections.content: Backend receives requests, checks logic, accesses databases, and prepares responses.

sections.heading: Frontend Displays Results
sections.content: Frontend receives server responses and updates the UI dynamically.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Depend On APIs
sections.content: Most modern apps work by continuously exchanging data between frontend and backend.

easyExample.title: Food Ordering Example
easyExample.content: Frontend is the waiter taking orders, backend is the kitchen preparing food, and the response is the delivered meal.

lessons.title: What Is API?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: An API allows different applications or systems to communicate with each other.

sections.heading: Why APIs Exist
sections.content: Frontend and backend need a structured way to exchange data safely.

sections.heading: APIs Define Rules
sections.content: APIs define what data can be requested and how responses should look.

sections.heading: Real World API Usage
sections.content: Weather apps, payment systems, login systems, and social media all use APIs.

sections.heading: Frontend Uses APIs Constantly
sections.content: Whenever frontend needs server data, it usually sends API requests.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Menu Example
easyExample.content: A menu defines what customers can order. APIs define what frontend can request.

summary: Most modern apps rely on APIs

lessons.title: What Is Database?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: A database stores and manages application data.

sections.heading: Why Databases Exist
sections.content: Applications need permanent storage for users, products, messages, and other information.

sections.heading: What Databases Store
sections.content: Databases store login data, profiles, posts, transactions, and application records.

sections.heading: Backend Connects To Database
sections.content: Frontend cannot directly access databases safely, so backend handles communication.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Depend On Data
sections.content: Social media, ecommerce, banking, and AI systems all rely heavily on databases.

easyExample.title: Library Example
easyExample.content: A database works like a library storing books in organized sections for easy access.

summary: Modern apps depend on stored data

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: A fullstack application combines frontend, backend, APIs, and databases together.

sections.heading: Frontend Starts Interaction
sections.content: Users interact with frontend interfaces like forms, buttons, and pages.

sections.heading: Frontend Sends API Request
sections.content: Frontend requests data or actions from backend servers.

sections.heading: Backend Processes Logic
sections.content: Backend checks authentication, processes requests, and communicates with databases.

sections.heading: Database Stores Information
sections.content: Database saves or retrieves required information.

sections.heading: Response Returns To Frontend
sections.content: Backend sends response back and frontend updates the UI dynamically.

easyExample.title: Instagram Login Example
easyExample.content: You enter login details on frontend, backend verifies them using database, and the app opens your account if valid.
